title: PilotTrace: offline validation and block scoring of 512-value numeric trace frames
description:
PilotTrace validates and deterministically scores caller-mapped numeric trace data supplied as UTF-8 JSON. Each accepted frame holds exactly 512 finite values, split into 16 contiguous blocks of 32. Each block is scored as 0.45*max|x| + 0.35*RMS(x) + 0.20*mean|x| and flagged when the score reaches a threshold frozen in the run manifest. The report keeps rejected-frame indices and reasons, SHA-256 hashes of the exact inputs, every block score and the flagged blocks; when boolean labels are supplied, it adds descriptive frame-classification metrics for the labelled frames only.

Scope: PilotTrace applies no preprocessing or calibration and makes no external connections. It is not an alarm, safety or process-control system, and a replay demonstrates input compatibility and deterministic arithmetic, not detection performance. Examples and tests use SYNTHETIC data.

Usage: Python 3.11 or later, standard library only. Run python3 tools/make_example.py and then python3 -m pilottrace --trace examples/sample_trace.json ... as shown in the README; a single-file version is also provided. Tests: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v (run in CI on Python 3.11 to 3.13).

Citation: cite the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23187278 for all versions, or the version DOI of the release you used. Source code: github.com/sparkainlp-x/pilottrace. Licence: AGPL-3.0-only; commercial licensing is available (see COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md).
